newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine o/night rate rises on weekend covering.
newsitem.headline: Philippine o/night rate rises on weekend covering.

text.p: * Money market unaffected by Ramos health condition
The Philippine overnight money nudged higher at 11.125 percent from Friday's average of 10.8125 percent due to the usual weekend covering, traders said.
Banks have to cover their reserve deficiencies over the weekend on Mondays.
Traders said reports that President Fidel Ramos underwent surgery of carotid earlier in the day did not create panic in the market, as it did in the equities and foreign exchange markets.
"The market is relatively liquid," one trader said, adding that most of the borrowers were small banks which were not able to beef up their deposit base for the year-end window-dressing.
He added that the market was expecting about one billion peso net inflow from maturing Treasury bills later this week.
Turnover in the interbank call market was heavy with 30.558 billion pesos changing hands with done rates ranging from 10.8125 to 11.5 percent.
The secondary Treasury bill market was quiet as traders await the results of the weekly auction.
Traders were expecting rates to remain sideways with the average rates drifting within 10 basis points.
Three-month bills were being bid between 11.45 and 11.75 and offered between 11.425 and 11.60 percent.
Six-month bills were being bought between 11.60 to 11.9 percent, and sold between 11.675 and 11.75 percent.
Three-month bills were being bid between 12.10 to 12.25 percent, and offered between 12.00 to 12.75 percent.
